display.purpose: The station name in the board header only; clamp(26px, 7.4vw, 40px) under 820px.

headline.purpose: Section heads on the line (Projects, Skills).

title.purpose: Station names in each station head; 24px under 820px. The qualifier beneath (Habit RPG · iOS, Live · Rails) is 14px/500/0.04em in Light 2.

board.purpose: The three section links under the route map.

small-headline.purpose: The route-map title; the same 22px numbers the header badge.

line-name.purpose: Skill line names in the lines-serving list, terminal names on the map, and the indicator's current code (18px/900 in rose).

body.purpose: Paragraphs at a 62ch measure; 16px under 820px. Station copy in Light 2.

name.purpose: Station names under the map and exit button labels; 16px for live stations and on mobile; wraps at 13px (terminals 15px, live 14px) between 820 and 1100px.

stack.purpose: Stack chips after their coloured square; the station qualifier shares the size at 500.

sub.purpose: The English second line on every section heading (Station information, All stations, Connecting lines), inset 0.6em and raised 0.25em, in Light 3; the untracked second line under the next-station links; the indicator's station name at 700 in white.

meta.purpose: The indicator strip's base size and its Next <station> text at 75% white.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels: fact keys, NOW AT and NEXT on the indicator, the map's App Store / Live · Rails sub-labels (0.06em); the untracked ← → ride key hints share the 11px step at 50%.

code.purpose: Numbers in the ringed square; line letter at 0.72em raised; scales 16/17/20/22px with the square.

shadows.name: route-glow
shadows.purpose: The rose halo on the map's lit segment, the lit rail and the current station mark only (--glow). The dim line ahead of the train never glows.

shadows.name: ticket-lift
shadows.purpose: The CV ticket at rest; hover 0 12px 24px -10px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8).

shadows.name: indicator-lift
shadows.purpose: The sticky in-car indicator strip; the 1px ring is its bezel.

shadows.name: object-lift
shadows.purpose: The terminal icons on the map, the 48px station icon and the portrait.

shadows.name: phone-lift
shadows.purpose: Screenshots and the trailer video; the ring keeps a black app screen legible on navy.

shadows.name: train-halo
shadows.purpose: The white light of the train glyph while it is moving only; off at rest and under reduced motion.

shadows.name: headlight
shadows.value: linear-gradient(to right, rgba(255, 162, 31, 0.45), rgba(255, 162, 31, 0)); 80px × 24px ahead of the nose; clip-path: polygon(0 40%, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 60%)
shadows.purpose: The amber beam ahead of the moving train on the map; nose-down (rail, and map under 820px) it is 24px × 80px, to bottom, polygon(40% 0, 60% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%). Hidden under reduced motion.

shadows.name: mark-halo
shadows.purpose: Every station mark; the current one appends route-glow.

shadows.name: interchange-ring
shadows.purpose: Double ring on a terminal's station code, at every width.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The shared easing for state transitions, the mark arrival and both opening keyframes.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The decelerating ease for the doors pulse and the headlight fade.

motion.name: spring
motion.value: Spring(response, ratio = 1): k = (2π / response)², c = 2 · ratio · √k; semi-implicit Euler, four substeps per frame, dt capped at 50ms; settled when |v| < 0.5 and |x − target| < 0.5
motion.purpose: The one model that moves the train: critically damped so it never overshoots a station, always re-targeted from its current position so a scroll, tap or key mid-ride redirects it without a jump. Under prefers-reduced-motion the spring sets its value instantly.

motion.name: rail-ride
motion.value: spring, response 0.45s; target = the rail point 38% down the viewport, re-targeted on every scroll (rAF-throttled) and reset on resize
motion.purpose: The rail train following the reader; it drives the lit rail, the is-here / is-passed classes and the indicator text each frame.

motion.name: map-ride
motion.value: spring, response 0.55s over stop indices, interpolating dock points (desktop x = code.left − 8 − 80; mobile y = code.top − 8 − 80)
motion.purpose: The map train riding to the station being read (on announce) or the station tapped (with the doors pulse); it scales the map's lit segment to its nose each frame.

motion.name: ride-scroll
motion.value: window.scrollTo({ top: mark centre − 38% of the viewport height + 2px, behavior: smooth })
motion.purpose: A tap on a map stop or a ← → / j k key press scrolls so the station's mark lands under the rail train; behavior auto under reduced motion.

motion.name: rail-light
motion.value: transform: scaleY(train y / rail height), set each frame by the rail spring
motion.purpose: The lit rail extending to the train's position; no transition under reduced motion.

motion.name: map-light
motion.value: transform: scaleX((train x + 80) / line width) (scaleY on the vertical map), set each frame by the map spring
motion.purpose: The map line lit as far as the train's nose, dim beyond it.

motion.name: doors
motion.value: 420ms ease-out; scale 1 → 1.14 at 35% → 1; is-boarding held 450ms by script
motion.purpose: The station code pulsing once as the doors open when the map train settles at a tapped stop; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: headlight-fade
motion.purpose: The headlight beam appearing as the train starts to move and fading as it settles; the white halo switches with the same class.

motion.name: line-draw
motion.value: 1100ms both; scaleX(0) to scaleX(1) from the left (scaleY from the top under 820px)
motion.purpose: The map line drawing itself on load; only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: stop-light
motion.value: 520ms both, delay 260ms + i × 70ms; opacity 0 to 1, translateY(6px) to none, brightness(2.2) to 1
motion.purpose: Each map stop lighting in sequence on load; only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: mark-arrive
motion.purpose: A station mark filling rose and scaling 1.25 when it becomes the current station.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Ticket rise and map-code scale 1.06 on hover (fine pointers) and focus.

narrative.overview:
The whole portfolio is one Tokyo transit line, read on the LCD above the train door at night. The page is deep navy glass; everything that was ink on enamel is now light on glass: near-white text, a single rose route line that enters at the route map, runs down the left edge of every section and closes the page as the footer's top rule. Every project is a numbered station on that line (A01 to A11); the two App Store apps are the terminals, drawn larger and double-ringed as interchanges. Reading the page is riding the line, and there is one train, seen twice. On the route map a side-view train glyph (80×24, light body, rose roof stripe, lit windows, amber headlamp) sits on the line and docks just short of each station sign; tap a station and it rides there on a critically damped spring while the page scrolls so that station's mark lands under the train on the rail. On the vertical rail the same glyph, nose down, follows the reader to a point 38% down the viewport, lighting the rail behind it and announcing every mark it passes on the in-car display strip. The line is lit only as far as the train has come, on the map and on the rail alike; the display lights up on load (the map line draws itself, the stations light one by one); the passed stations keep their rose ring.

Density is signage density. Nothing is boxed; information sits directly on the glass and is organised by the line, by station codes in ringed rounded squares, and by weight. Headings carry a second, smaller line the way every platform sign does, in the same face, one step down and tracked; all copy is English (the earlier Japanese sub-labels were removed on 2026-10-09 at the owner's request). Icons are pictograms: stroked SVG at 1.8px, round-capped, never glyph fonts. The Tokyo Metro and Toei line colours appear, lightened so they read as lit segments on the display, but strictly to name the skill lines (Rails is Marunouchi red, PostgreSQL is Mita blue, Swift is Ginza orange); the page itself has exactly one colour, Asakusa-Line rose, and light is rationed: the route glows where it is lit, the train's headlamp and halo light up only while it moves, and nothing else glows.

Rejected on the evidence of the build: the category arrangement of hero-name-over-avatar and a grid of equal project cards. There are no cards, no eyebrows or kickers, no decorative dividers, no second display face, and no glow on anything that is not the route or the moving train.
keyCharacteristics: Navy glass ground, near-white light as "ink"; one route colour carries the page; nine lightened Tokyo line colours only ever name a skill line, and Ginza orange alone doubles as the train's headlamp.
No cards and no boxes; the rose line, the station marks and heavy weight do the structuring.
A single signage face (Zen Kaku Gothic New) at four weights, heavy for names, light-tracked small caps for labels; English copy only.
Station codes in rounded squares with a rose ring on a slightly lighter navy fill.
One train, seen twice: the same 80×24 SVG glyph rides the route map between station signs and, rotated nose-down, rides the rail with the reader.

The route is the only thing that glows, and only where it is lit: the map's lit segment, the lit rail and the current station mark carry the rose halo; the moving train carries an amber headlight beam and a white halo; everything else is matte.
Motion is the train: two critically damped springs (rail 0.45s, map 0.55s, no overshoot) plus the opening light-up; every other transition is a 100–220ms state change.

rules.name: The One Route Rule
rules.body: The page has one accent, Asakusa rose, and it is spent only on the line (lit or dim), the train's roof stripe, the rings and marks, the dots, the indicator code, the one primary exit per station, link hover and selection. No heading, background or secondary button is rose; the ticket in the header is light, not rose, so the CV reads as the thing you hold rather than part of the line.

rules.name: The Lines Name Lines Rule
rules.body: A Tokyo line colour may only identify a skill line, as a 14px square or an 18px band beside its name. It never fills a button, tints a background, colours a heading or decorates anything. The single exception is Ginza orange as the train's headlamp and beam: a lamp on the one object that moves, not a label.

rules.name: The Second Line Rule
rules.body: Every section heading and every station title that has a qualifier carries its second line in the same face, smaller, lighter and tracked, in English; it is part of the sign, never a kicker above it.

rules.name: The Heavy Names Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a station (header, section heads, station titles, map names at terminals, next-station links, line names, the indicator code) is 900 weight. Body, legends and labels never exceed 700.

rules.name: The Objects Cast Rule
rules.body: Only objects cast shadows; text blocks, sections, lists and the page never do. If a new element is not something you could hold in front of the display, it gets no shadow.

rules.name: The Light Rule
rules.body: The rose glow is applied only to the route, and only where it is lit: the map's lit segment, the lit rail and the active station mark. The dim line ahead of the train never glows. The train lights up only while it moves: amber headlight ahead, white halo on the glyph. Everything else is matte; a glow on a button, a heading, a chip or a card is a violation, not a variant.

rules.name: The Line Is The Rule Rule
rules.body: Structural rules are the route line itself: the 13px map line, the 10px rail, the 10px terminus top edge. The next-station board carries no rule and nothing stacks with hairlines. The only other 1px lines are on objects, not between content: the bezel rings on the indicator and the phones, the divider inside the indicator strip before `Next`, and the outlines of the `kbd` key hints.

dos: Do keep Asakusa rose (`route`) for the line, the train's roof stripe, the rings and marks, the dots, the indicator code, the one primary exit per station, link hover and selection; use dim rose (`route-dim`) only for the route switched off (the unlit map line and rail ahead of the train, the unreached mark ring, the scrollbar).
